questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of $6a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 4 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 2 \\ -3 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 & -3 \\ 4 & -2 & 2 & -6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}15 & 30 \\ 30 & 60\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 20\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}15 & 30 & 10 \\ 30 & 60 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}15 & 30 & 10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{2}{3}-2{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}-2{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
6a+\frac{b}{c}=6\cdot \frac{2}{3}+\frac{(-2)}{1}=2.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $A$ and vector $b$ shown above. If the general least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 \\ b \\ c\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}a \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R
$$

what is the value of $a+2b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -8 & 2 \\ -8 & 12 & -4 \\ 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -8 & 2 & 0 \\ -8 & 12 & -4 & 2 \\ 2 & -4 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ -8 & 12 & -4 & 2 \\ 6 & -8 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 & 6\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & -4 & 4 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has two pivot columns (the $1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. From the second equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{2}=\frac{3}{2}+{x}_{3}.
$$

Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

$$
2{x}_{1}-4(\frac{3}{2}+{x}_{3})+2{x}_{3}=-2\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=2+{x}_{3}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2+{x}_{3} \\ \frac{3}{2}+{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+2b+c=1+2\cdot \frac{3}{2}+0=4.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}=3 \\ -2{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=1 \\ {x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}=-5\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $12a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 1 \\ 3 & 6 & -3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -18 \\ -18 & 54\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ 30\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -18 & -10 \\ -18 & 54 & 30\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -18 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{5}{3}+3{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{3}+3{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{5}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
12a+\frac{b}{c}=12\cdot (-\frac{5}{3})+\frac{3}{1}=-17.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=3 \\ 6{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=1 \\ 3{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=-2\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $-4a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 6 & -2 \\ 3 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 6 & 3 \\ 1 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}54 & -18 \\ -18 & 6\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}54 & -18 & -9 \\ -18 & 6 & 3\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}54 & -18 & -9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:=\frac{1}{9}{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=-\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{3}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{6} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
-4a+\frac{b}{c}=-4\cdot (-\frac{1}{6})+\frac{(\frac{1}{3})}{1}=1.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
\{\begin{aligned}-{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=2 \\ {x}_{1}-4{x}_{2}=2 \\ 2{x}_{1}-8{x}_{2}=4\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear equations shown above. If the general least-squares solution of the system is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R
$$

what is the value of $3a+\frac{b}{c}?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we write our system in matrix form as $Ax=b,$ where 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 2 & -8\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$

The least-squares solution of $Ax=b$ satisfies the corresponding normal equation:

$$
{A}^{T}\,Ax={A}^{T}b
$$

Notice that the columns of $A$ are linearly dependent. So first, let's write down the normal equation in matrix form:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & -4 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-1 & 4 \\ 1 & -4 \\ 2 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 1 & 2 \\ 4 & -4 & -8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & -24 \\ -24 & 96\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -32\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the final matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}6 & -24 & 8 \\ -24 & 96 & -32\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}6 & -24 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
{x}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}+4{x}_{2}.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3}+4{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{4}{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
3a+\frac{b}{c}=3\cdot \frac{4}{3}+\frac{4}{1}=8.
$$
